abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) improve cancer outcomes but can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs) that compromise treatment. Using FAERS real-world data, we developed a two-layer network algorithm to identify irAE-associated lncRNAs (irAEsLncs) across 18 cancer types. The irAEsLnc network showed organ-specific patterns and cancer-specific irAE susceptibility, while irAEsLncs were associated with immune infiltration, inflammatory responses, immune activation, and checkpoint molecules. Single-cell analysis of ICI-induced colitis linked irAEsLncs to inflammatory macrophage and T cell states and metabolic reprogramming. irAEsLnc-derived signatures independently predicted prognosis and responses to targeted therapy and immunotherapy, with ALAL-1/CD80/MEF2C predicting ICI efficacy in lung adenocarcinoma. Knockdown of ALAL-1 and SEC61G-DT suppressed tumor cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and macrophage-mediated inflammation. These findings connect irAE-associated lncRNAs with toxicity and antitumor immunity and support their potential as biomarkers for treatment stratification.

title: Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy for stage IIIA-B non-small cell lung cancer invading pulmonary artery or main bronchus.
authors: Wang S, Zhou Y, Hu S et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Centrally located non-small cell lung cancer involving the pulmonary artery or main bronchus is often considered unresectable or requires sleeve resection or pneumonectomy. We evaluated outcomes after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by surgery or radiotherapy in this population.
METHODS: We included patients with stage IIIA-B non-small cell lung cancer involving the pulmonary artery or main bronchus who received neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy. Among patients without disease progression after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, event-free survival and overall survival were compared between those treated with surgery and radiotherapy. The association between adjuvant immunotherapy and survival outcomes was also examined. Survival was analyzed using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox proportional hazards regression.
RESULTS: A total of 159 patients met the eligibility criteria. The 2-year event-free survival and overall survival rates for the entire cohort were 66.4% and 89.3%, respectively. Among patients without disease progression after neoadjuvant therapy, the hazard ratio for surgery versus radiotherapy was 0.33 (95% confidence interval, 0.16-0.70; P = .004) for event-free survival and 1.28 (95% confidence interval, 0.15-11.04; P = .822) for overall survival. Overall, 92 patients (75.4%) underwent surgery; 13 (14.1%) underwent pneumonectomy, 91 (98.9%) achieved R0 resection, and no patient died within 90 days after surgery. Adjuvant immunotherapy was not significantly associated with event-free survival or overall survival in either treatment group.
CONCLUSION: Among selected patients with centrally located stage IIIA-B non-small cell lung cancer, neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by surgery was associated with favorable event-free survival. Only a small proportion of surgical patients underwent pneumonectomy.

title: A Prospective Cohort Study of PD-1 Monoclonal Antibody Combined With Ipilimumab N01 and Chemotherapy in Perioperative Treatment of Resectable Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
summary:
This multicenter, prospective, randomized controlled study aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of different durations of neoadjuvant treatment with a PD-1 inhibitor, ipilimumab, and chemotherapy in patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). A total of 90 treatment-naïve patients with clinical stage IIA (primary tumor \>4 cm) to stage IIIB (limited to resectable N2 disease) NSCLC will be enrolled and randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to Cohort A (n=45) or Cohort B (n=45).

Patients in Cohort A will receive two cycles of a PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy and one cycle of ipilimumab, whereas patients in Cohort B will receive four cycles of a PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy and two cycles of ipilimumab. The PD-1 inhibitor will be administered intravenously at 200 mg every three weeks, and ipilimumab at 1 mg/kg every six weeks. Chemotherapy regimens will be selected according to histological subtype: pemetrexed plus carboplatin or cisplatin for non-squamous NSCLC, and nab-paclitaxel plus carboplatin or cisplatin for squamous NSCLC.

Following neoadjuvant treatment, eligible patients will undergo curative-intent surgery within 22-42 days after the last treatment dose. Investigator-selected adjuvant therapy will begin 29-42 days after surgery. Tumor assessments will be performed according to RECIST version 1.1, with postoperative follow-up for up to five years.

The primary endpoint is the pathological complete response (pCR) rate, with treatment safety also being evaluated.

title: Deep learning-based detection and classification of airway nodules on CT for early medical intervention.
authors: Liu S, Yi P, Fan Y et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Airway lesions are common CT findings in interval and post-screen lung cancers; however, airway nodules are frequently overlooked. Robust artificial intelligence (AI) tools for characterizing airway nodules remain limited. This study aimed to develop and evaluate deep learning-based models for the detection and classification of airway nodules on low-dose CT(LDCT) as a second-reading tool.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: 1813 segmental and more proximal airway nodules were retrospectively identified from 1107 LDCT of 1043 participants. A sphere-based center-points matching network, first used to establish a lung nodule detection model, was transferred to airway nodules and enhanced by incorporating coordinate and multiscale attention. The model was trained on 907 proximal airway nodules and independently tested on 738 proximal nodules across four hospitals. The clinical utility of the AI tool was evaluated through human-AI interaction. For nodule classification, a 3D SEResNeXt101-based model was trained, validated and tested using 286 airway nodules (121 benign, 165 malignant) with a 6:2:2 split and evaluated in an independent testing dataset.
RESULTS: On the independent testing set, the detection model achieved a high sensitivity of 73.7%. Human-AI interaction demonstrated AI assistance significantly improved radiologists' performance, increasing sensitivity from 39.5% to 72.9% and F1-score from 49.4% to 77.2%, while reducing diagnosis time from 83.8 s to 61.8 s. The classification model showed high sensitivities of 82.1%, 71.4%, 94.3%, 72.7% and specificities of 62.7%, 73.9%, 73.9%, 87.5% across multicenter training, validation, testing and independent testing sets, respectively.
CONCLUSION: This AI system significantly enhances the detection and classification of proximal airway nodules, guiding early medical intervention.
KEY POINTS: Question Improved early detection and classification of airway nodules are critical for lung cancer mortality reduction, but AI-based CAD systems targeting airway nodules remain scarce. Findings The DL models for detection and classification of proximal airway nodules on chest CT were developed and assisted radiologists to achieve higher detection accuracy. Critical Relevance Statement The clinical applications of the proposed DL-based system for detecting and classifying proximal airway nodules on chest CT scans help radiologists reduce missed/delayed diagnoses and shorten diagnostic time as a second-reading tool, guiding medical intervention and improving clinical outcomes.

title: Comparison of Two Deep Learning Models and Their Combination for 1-year Lung Cancer Detection in Two Screening Cohorts.
authors: Reeves AP, Mozafary M, Hashemi A et al.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the performance of Sybil, a Medical Open Network for Artificial Intelligence (MONAI)-based nodule model, and their combination for 1-year lung cancer detection in two screening cohorts: the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST) and the Pamplona International Early Lung Cancer Action Program (P-IELCAP). Materials and Methods Baseline low-dose CT (LDCT) examinations from the NLST and the P-IELCAP were analyzed. A prespecified OR-stacked composite model combining Sybil, a MONAI-based nodule model, and a safety-net rule (MONAI-detected nodule > 6 mm with detection confidence > 0.95) was developed and evaluated for 1-year lung cancer detection. Model discrimination was assessed by using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), and operating-point performance metrics were calculated. Results A total of 5110 baseline LDCT examinations were analyzed, including 2343 from NLST and 2767 from P-IELCAP, with 65 lung cancers diagnosed within 1 year. Mean age, mean pack-years, and percentage of female participants were 61.6 years ± 5.1 (SD), 57.3 pack-years ± 24.8, and 39.4% (923 of 2343), respectively, in NLST and 56.0 years ± 9.5, 34.4 pack-years ± 21.5, and 28.6% (791 of 2767), respectively, in P-IELCAP. Lung cancer incidence (per 1000 person-years) was higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (17.7 vs 8.7; P = .006). Mean Sybil 1-year lung cancer probabilities (scaled by 1000 for presentation) were also higher in NLST than in P-IELCAP (16.4 vs 9.9; P < .01). Sybil achieved an AUC of 0.93 in both cohorts, whereas the MONAI-based model achieved AUCs of 0.90 in NLST and 0.79 in P-IELCAP. The composite model missed two of 65 1-year lung cancers while correctly classifying 2731 of 4965 (55.0%) noncancer examinations as negative, yielding a sensitivity of 63 of 65 (96.9%) and a positive predictive value of 63 of 2297 (2.7%). Conclusion For 1-year lung cancer detection with LDCT, the composite AI model achieved high sensitivity while maintaining acceptable specificity. Keywords: Applications-CT, Thorax, Pulmonary, Sybil, MONAI, NLST, P-IELCAP, Lung Cancer, Low Dose Computed Tomography Supplemental material is available for this article. © RSNA, 2026.

title: Qualitative Insights From Public Interviews in the United Kingdom on the Acceptability of Risk-Based Eligibility Criteria for Lung Cancer Screening.
authors: Katsampouris E, Hutton G, Scott SE et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Targeted lung cancer screening programmes in the United Kingdom use multivariable risk models to identify high-risk individuals. However, public acceptability of targeting screening by risk using eligibility criteria, such as age and smoking history, remains unclear, including the psychological and behavioural consequences of eligibility disclosure.
AIM: To explore UK public attitudes toward the acceptability of current risk-based eligibility criteria for lung cancer screening and the anticipated psychological and behavioural responses to eligibility disclosure.
METHODS: A qualitative study was conducted as the second phase of a sequential explanatory design. Semi-structured telephone interviews were held with 28 UK adults aged 45-77 years between January-April 2024. Participants were purposively sampled for diversity in demographics, smoking history, and prior acceptability questionnaire responses. Interviews were analysed using applied thematic analysis informed by the Theoretical Framework of Acceptability.
RESULTS: Criteria were generally acceptable when perceived as evidence-based and logical, particularly age and smoking history. However, participants expected flexibility, suggested expanding inclusion criteria and had concerns about fairness and discrimination especially regarding ethnicity and education. Eligibility was anticipated to motivate screening attendance but also cause worry; the prospect of ineligibility often led to feelings of exclusion, anxiety, and disappointment. Participants emphasised the need for clear, evidence-based communication of the rationale and individual risk, alongside alternative options or support for those who are ineligible.
CONCLUSIONS: Clear and transparent communication of the rationales underpinning eligibility criteria, provided by the screening programme and trusted health professionals, are essential for improving public acceptability and individual understanding of eligibility status. These strategies should also mitigate against potential stigma, perceived discrimination, and over-reassurance, while ensuring appropriate safety-netting and risk management for those who are ineligible. Tailored messaging and pathways may optimise engagement, trust, and psychological wellbeing within lung cancer screening programmes.
PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: The research team sought the views of eight public and patient representatives with lung cancer experience (either personally or being a carer) during study conception. They endorsed the research objectives, helped to develop participant-facing interview questions and gave feedback on the appropriateness of the design, agreeing that in-depth interviews would best capture perceptions of the acceptability of risk-based eligibility criteria.

title: Case Finding for COPD in Nottingham and District (C FIND COPD). A Pilot Study of Uptake, Acceptability and Diagnostic Yield in a One-Stop Assessment Following Lung Cancer Screening.
authors: Burzic A, Hamrouni M, Porte J et al.
journal: Int J Chron Obstruct Pulmon Dis
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Several lung cancer screening (LCS) programmes have identified a high prevalence of people with new (often pre-bronchodilator) airflow obstruction, but demonstrable translation into confirmed chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) diagnosis is limited. We evaluated a community-based, one-stop, post-bronchodilator case-finding and initial management pathway following LCS.
METHODS: Participants undergoing low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) as part of a LCS programme who reported respiratory symptoms were invited to attend a community-based assessment. The pathway included post-bronchodilator spirometry, clinical review and initial management delivered within a single encounter. The primary outcomes were uptake and new clinical diagnosis of COPD. Secondary outcomes included symptom burden, relationship to CT findings, socioeconomic variation and participant-reported experience.
RESULTS: Of 2860 invitation letters issues, 529 (18.5%) invitees participated; a further 33 participants self-presented. Of 562 participants overall, 486 completed spirometry, including 407 without a prior COPD diagnosis. Of these, 100 (25%) participants received a new clinical diagnosis of COPD, mainly with mild-to-moderate airflow obstruction. Among participants with a COPD Assessment Test (CAT) score ≥10, Medical Research Council (MRC) dyspnoea score ≥2, or clinician-defined respiratory symptoms, 35%, 34%, and 38%, respectively, had airflow obstruction. Moderate-to-severe CT emphysema was highly specific but poorly sensitive for airflow obstruction. We detected no significant difference in new COPD diagnosis across deprivation quintiles. Participant-reported experience was very positive.
CONCLUSION: A community-based, one-stop pathway following LCS can identify clinically meaningful COPD diagnosis in symptomatic individuals. This single encounter approach addresses a key gap in current LCS-linked pathways, maximising opportunities for case finding and supporting accessible, patient-centred diagnostic services.

title: The metabolic dependency on GLUT3 mediates smoking-induced NSCLC progression.
authors: Cheng FJ, Shen YC, Chen BR et al.
abstract: Cigarette smoking is strongly associated with aggressive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet the mechanisms linking smoke exposure to metabolic reprogramming remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated clinical, molecular, and functional analyses to define a smoking-associated metabolic axis in NSCLC. Lung cancer patients with a smoking history exhibited significantly higher tumor 18F-FDG uptake than never-smokers, suggesting an association between smoking exposure and increased tumor metabolic activity. Consistently, chronic exposure of NSCLC cells to cigarette smoke extract (CSE) or its ingredient benzo[α]pyrene (B[α]P) increased glucose uptake, glycolysis, ATP production, and malignant phenotypes, including proliferation, migration, and sphere formation. Mechanistically, GLUT3 protein, but not mRNA, was selectively upregulated in smoke-exposed tumors and cell models, suggesting post-transcriptional regulation. We identified miR-146a as a direct suppressor of GLUT3 through binding to its 3'UTR and found that cigarette smoke markedly reduced miR-146a expression. Smoker-derived NSCLC tumors exhibited lower miR-146a expression and higher GLUT3 levels, which were inversely correlated and associated with poor overall survival. Restoration of miR-146a reduced GLUT3 expression, glucose uptake, and tumor cell proliferation, supporting a central role for the miR-146a/GLUT3 axis in smoking-induced metabolic reprogramming. (-)Gallocatechin ((-)GC), a naturally occurring catechin, is further identified as a selective GLUT3 inhibitor and suppressed smoke-induced glucose uptake, tumor progression, and metastasis without detectable systemic toxicity. Collectively, these findings identify the miR-146a/GLUT3 axis as a key mechanism underlying smoking-driven metabolic reprogramming and establish GLUT3 as a potential metabolic target in NSCLC and other GLUT3-dependent malignancies.

title: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis is associated with reduced lung function independent of structural lung abnormalities.
authors: Harlianto NI, Oudkerk SF, de Jong PA et al.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) has been associated with lower lung volumes and function, but it is unknown whether this is due to structural lung disease. This study aimed to investigate DISH and reduced lung function and volume in relation to structural lung disease in individuals with long-term smoking history.
METHODS: Participants were included from the NELSON lung cancer screening trial. Structural lung abnormalities were automatically quantified (emphysema, airway wall thickness, and air trapping), or visually assessed (interstitial lung abnormalities, bronchiectasis, centrolobular emphysema) by two chest radiologists. Multivariate linear regression analyses were performed with adjustment for participant factors and structural lung disease.
RESULTS: Among 3514 subjects (100% male, mean age 60.4 years), DISH was present in 241 (6.7%). Individuals with DISH had lower prevalence of Respiratory Bronchiolitis Interstitial Lung Disease (5%vs. 10.4%, p = 0.04) and of centrilobular emphysema (3.3%vs. 7.6%, p = 0.009), but greater airway wall thickness (2.6 vs. 2.4 mm, p < 0.001). In multivariate linear regression analyses, DISH subjects had a 4.4% lower FEV1 (95%CI: -7.1% to -1.7%), 150 ml lower FEV1 (95%CI: -160, -140 ml), 4.0% lower predicted FVC (95%CI: -6.2%, -1.7%), 170 ml lower FVC (95%CI: -280, -70 ml) and 210 ml lower CT measured lung volume (95%CI: -40, -1 ml), compared to subjects without DISH.
CONCLUSION: In long-term smokers, DISH was associated with lower lung function and volumes, not explained by structural lung abnormalities on CT. These findings suggest that DISH may be an extrinsic factor contributing to reduced lung function as a result of thoracic cage stiffening.

title: Dosimetric risk factors for therapy-related pneumonitis in patients with immunotherapy plus chemotherapy concurrent thoracic radiotherapy.
authors: Lu Y, Wang Y, Han G et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Combining immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) with chemoradiotherapy is being actively investigated to improve clinical outcomes; however, this strategy may also increase the risk of treatment-related toxicities. This multicenter study aimed to identify clinical and dosimetric predictors of treatment-related pneumonitis (TRP) in this patient population, focusing on modifiable predictors of toxicity.
METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted on 69 patients with lung or esophageal cancer treated at three hospitals. All patients received concurrent ICIs, chemotherapy, and thoracic radiotherapy at a dose of 50-60 Gy (in 2 Gy fractions) using inverse-planned techniques. TRP was graded according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5.0. Logistic regression modeling and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis were employed for statistical evaluation.
RESULTS: Any-grade TRP occurred in 56.5% of patients. Grade 2-5 TRP occurred in 30.4%, 8.7%, 1.4%, and 0% of patients, respectively. Age (p = 0.01; OR = 1.1) and mean lung dose (MLD) (p = 0.02; OR = 2.4) independently contributed to the risk of any-grade TRP. Age (p = 0.03; OR = 1.1) and MLD (p = 0.04; OR = 1.7) were also identified as risk factors for grade 2+ TRP. Other parameters, such as lung V5, V10, V15, V20, and V30 were not significantly associated with TRP. ROC analysis identified 13.6 Gy as the optimal MLD threshold for predicting both any-grade and grade 2+ TRP.
CONCLUSIONS: MLD and age were associated with a higher risk of TRP in patients receiving concurrent chemoradiotherapy and ICIs. These findings may help inform revisions to lung dose constraints, although validation in large-scale prospective trials is warranted.

title: Cardiovascular biomarker phenotype associated with immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer: an exploratory blood transcriptome study.
authors: Ziemska-Legięcka J, Żeber-Lubecka N, Borucka M et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the management of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but their use is associated with potentially serious immune-related cardiotoxicity, often reflected by elevations in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Identifying patients at risk before treatment initiation remains a major clinical challenge. The aim of this study was to investigate whether peripheral blood transcriptomic profiles are associated with susceptibility to an ICI-related cardiac biomarker-defined phenotype.
METHODS: Peripheral blood RNA sequencing was performed in patients with advanced NSCLC receiving anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy (n=61) and in a control group with predominantly early-stage disease (n=29). Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses were used to characterize global and baseline transcriptomic differences, early treatment-related changes, and molecular signatures associated with NT-proBNP elevation and survival.
RESULTS: Despite substantial transcriptomic overlap (86.0% of genes shared), global analysis revealed significant differences between early- and advanced-stage disease, as demonstrated by PCA and PERMANOVA. Baseline comparison in patients who subsequently developed NT-proBNP elevation identified a small set of differentially expressed genes (n=9), indicating subtle pre-treatment differences in regulatory and signaling pathways. Early response analysis demonstrated modest transcriptional changes after the first ICI cycle, with enrichment analyses pointing to immune-related pathways, including leukocyte migration and cytokine signaling. NT-proBNP-defined phenotype was associated with exploratory differential gene expression patterns and enrichment of pathways related to T-cell activation and immune signaling. Exploratory survival-associated transcriptomic profiles were characterized by enrichment of pathways related to platelet activation, coagulation and cell adhesion.
CONCLUSION: Peripheral blood transcriptomic profiling reveals stage-dependent and clinically relevant transcriptomic patterns in NSCLC, including early immune-related transcriptional changes and signatures associated with a cardiovascular biomarker phenotype defined by NT-proBNP changes. Although these alterations are subtle, they highlight the potential of peripheral blood transcriptomic profiling to identify transcriptomic signatures associated with an NT-proBNP-defined cardiovascular biomarker phenotype. Given the exploratory nature of the analyses and the relatively small size of several subgroups, particularly the survival comparison, these findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent cohorts.

title: Pancreatic metastasis from thymic carcinoma diagnosed by endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition: a case report influencing therapeutic strategy.
authors: Maekawa N, Takahashi K, Nakao Y et al.
abstract: Pancreatic metastasis from thymic carcinoma is exceedingly rare and difficult to distinguish from primary pancreatic neoplasms based on imaging alone. We report a case of pancreatic and hepatic metastases from thymic carcinoma diagnosed by endoscopic ultrasound-guided tissue acquisition (EUS-TA), which directly influenced therapeutic management. A 74-year-old woman with a history of resected thymic carcinoma and hepatic metastasectomy presented with newly detected pancreatic and hepatic masses. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a hypoenhancing pancreatic lesion with heterogeneous enhancement. Although the findings were nonspecific, they were atypical for conventional pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma because the main pancreatic duct remained patent without upstream dilatation or pancreatic atrophy. EUS-TA using a 22-gauge Franseen needle provided sufficient tissue for histopathological and immunohistochemical evaluation. The pancreatic lesion showed morphological and immunohistochemical concordance with both the previously resected primary thymic carcinoma and hepatic metastasis, confirming metastatic disease. Histological diagnosis established systemic recurrence, avoided unnecessary pancreatic resection, and led to stereotactic body radiation therapy followed by systemic chemotherapy, resulting in tumor regression. This case highlights the pivotal role of EUS-TA in establishing an accurate diagnosis and guiding appropriate therapeutic management.

title: Risk estimates in BAP1 tumor predisposition syndrome using the Genotype-Restricted Likelihood (GRL) method.
authors: Lamure V, Veyrune L, Golmard L et al.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Germline BAP1 (likely) pathogenic variants ((L)PV) confer predisposition to uveal melanoma (UM), cutaneous melanoma (CM), renal cell carcinoma (RCC), and malignant mesothelioma (MM). Higher risks of lung cancer (LC) and breast cancer (BC) have been hypothesized with risk estimates using bias-correcting methods.
METHODS: We included 26 families with 90 heterozygotes for a germline BAP1 (L)PV. Cumulative risk (CR) and relative risk (RR) were estimated using the Genotype-Restricted Likelihood (GRL) method to correct for ascertainment bias.
RESULTS: The CR at 80 years are 7.3% (95% CI: 1.3-37.9) for UM, 16.1% (2.9-74.4) for CM, 49.4% (6-83.9) for RCC, 8.5% (2.5-73.8) for MM, 9.8% (6.5-55.9) for LC and 58.6 (19-91.8) for BC. Corresponding RR to population incidence at 50 and 80 years are respectively 383.4 (72.4-779.1) and 95.9 (17.3-501) for UM, 5.7 (1-24.4) and 8.2 (1.5-37.9) for CM, 61.1 (11.7-157) and 29.9 (3.7-50.8) for RCC, 7.5 (1.1-1530.7) and 55.7 (16.5-482) for MM, 1.4 (1-26.4) and 1.7 (1.1-9.6) for LC and 7.4 (1-17.2) and 4.7 (1.5-7.4) for BC.
CONCLUSION: These GRL-based tumor risk estimates for individuals with heterozygous BAP1 (L)PV will help guide clinical management and surveillance strategies. Further studies are needed to refine these values.

title: Composite Hemangioendothelioma with Concurrent Pyoderma Gangrenosum Treated with Pazopanib: A Case Report.
authors: Ishida T, Anzai M, Yonemoto N et al.
abstract: A 40-year-old man with an eight-year history of a cutaneous mass complicated by subsequent pyoderma gangrenosum developed systemic disease. Pleural fluid cytology initially suggested pleural mesothelioma (PM), whereas a subsequent subcutaneous biopsy was interpreted as epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE). Through a retrospective re-evaluation of previous skin specimens and comparison with current pathological findings, a final diagnosis of composite hemangioendothelioma (CHE) was established. Pazopanib (PAZ) achieved radiologically stable disease for five months; however, he died of progressive respiratory failure. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of extremely rare CHE and suggests that PAZ may have a limited therapeutic impact on advanced CHE with malignant pleural effusions.
